institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It is a well respected university, and I used to live in Paris some years ago - which made me want to come back, so that I could practice my french again.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say it was easy - both the information about going abroad from back home and from Sciences Po were difficult to understand completely, so there was always some uncertainty about if we were doing the right thing or if we had misunderstood something. But after all, it turned out well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro week where they gave us information about the different things that we needed to know, and Sciences Po sends out a lot uf mails, so that was helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is not easy to find housing in Paris and it is often very expensive. So you have to look early on other sites than airbnb, because airbnb is the most expensive I think - but also the easiest. If you book through an agency, you have to show them a lot of different papers proving that you will be able to pay the rent etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend it, but haven't lived on. campus, so I don't know how that is. Try to avoid the turist areas, they are often more expensive and you don't get the local feeling. A nice thing about being abroad is that you get to feel home in another city and have your local cafes and places that you go to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Not well organized in my opinion. It is a 2 days open window, and all the courses are gone within some minutes. And in a lot of cases you won’t be able to change courses afterwards, which criticizable when you have some obligatory courses from back home.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
They had an office open for a couple of hours one day during the first week of school where you could apply for changes, but that was it. 

It was helpful though that we got an introduction zoom meeting about how to apply for courses on the website and how the process was - because I wouldn't have been able to figure it out without that. So that was very nice, and they gave a lot of good recommendations on how to be tactical.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi - I got most of them I had to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared and have as many courses ready to choose as you can.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The students are very dedicated and the level is high in most of the courses, but the way it is organized is a bit like being back in highschool. Nice to try something else and be challenged, but also to much workload compared to what you get out of it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More like being in highschool at my host university. I like the teaching style more at UCPH - more well organized and you have more freedom as a student to think of your own, which I think is very important.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ASPO 25A11: Comparative Politics
ASPO 25A29: Comparative Social Policy in Europe
DSPO 25A02: European Integration and its challenges:The Euro, Migration and Populism
AHUM 25A15: Ethics of War and Peace
ASPO 25A27: Religion, Politics and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend this one: ASPO 25A27: Religion, Politics and Society - the best course I had and the professor is really amazing.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy a lot of essentials when you first arrive - or we had to buy a lot for the place that we stayed, because there was no towels etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to do your grocery - almost the same prices as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different. Both sports and art etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to museums. A lot of them are free if you are under 25 or a student at a french university. And walk! Everywhere, that's the best way to get to know the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out of the city. Go to Versailles or Marseille or something like that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy because it Paris, but the french way to do things can also be very different from the danish. Avoid going into bureaucratic stuff with the french system.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging, but it is a city where there are a lot of people, which can be a bit stressful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is history everywhere. Just walking around the city is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't get too stressed in the beginning about the workload. It will be fine, but you will have a lot to do throughout the semester.
But be organized and get your work done in a good time, because there will always be another assignment waiting.
Try to engage in class - a part of your grade is your oral participation, and class gets much better if you do that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the campus - there are a lot of libraries where you can study.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Get to experience another university very different from the one back home. And meeting so many dedicated students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing in academic English in the beginning. But it gets better.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
